paras.text: Annex 1 NBB - ConfidentialNBB - Confidential Publication of the decision of the National Bank of Belgium concerning Paynovate SA pursuant to Article 98/1 in conjunction with Article 135 §3 of the Act of 18 September 2017 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing and on restriction of the use of cash The National Bank of Belgium (hereinafter the “Bank”), in its capacity as the authority responsible for supervising compliance with the provisions laid down by and pursuant to the Act of 18 September 2017 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing and on restriction of the use of cash (hereinafter the “Anti-Money Laundering Act”) and the Regulation of the National Bank of Belgium of 21 November 2017 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, approved by the Royal Decree of 10 December 2017 (hereinafter the “NBB Regulation”), has carried out an assessment of the system put in place by Paynovate SA to comply with the Anti-Money Laundering Act and the NBB Regulation.

The checks carried out by the NBB led it to conclude that the due diligence applied by Paynovate SA presents serious shortcomings with respect to several key obligations set out in the Anti-Money Laundering Act and the NBB Regulation, specifically in relation to: (a) customer identification and identity verification (Articles 26, 27 and 30 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act and Article 12, point (1), second paragraph, of the NBB Regulation); (b) identification of customer characteristics as well as the purpose and nature of business relationships (Article 34 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act); and
(c) ongoing due diligence with regard to business relationships and transactions (Article 35 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act and Articles 17 and 22 of the NBB Regulation).

Pursuant to Article 94, first paragraph, point (3), and second paragraph of the Anti-Money Laundering Act, the Bank decided on 17 November 2026 to prohibit Paynovate SA from accepting new customers in connection with both its payment account and acquiring services until the aforementioned shortcomings have been effectively and permanently resolved. By way of exception, in the cases exhaustively listed in the decision, establishing a business relationship with a new customer that poses a low or standard risk in relation to money laundering and terrorist financing remains authorised, subject to compliance with strict conditions, reinforced prior checks and specific monitoring obligations imposed by the Bank.
